ranked.intervention: Incorporate 200 nm ZrO2 particles into the ceramic sealant matrix of the solid oxide fuel cell to form a rigid percolation framework that acts as heterogeneous nucleation centers for diopside

ranked.mechanism: Formation of a rigid percolation framework by 200 nm particles that improves local sintering and promotes pore closure, thereby distributing thermal stress uniformly.
ranked.intervention: Incorporate 200 nm ZrO2 particles into the ceramic electrolyte or interlayer microstructure at an optimized weight fraction to form a continuous rigid percolation network, and use SEM-based quantitative image analysis of the percolation framework continuity as the single predictive microstructure measurement for 1000-cycle survival.

ranked.mechanism: High valence dopant mediation reduces lattice strain and thermal stress accumulation during thermal cycling by promoting a more flexible lattice structure via oxygen vacancy formation, thereby delaying crack initiation in the ceramic electrolyte.
ranked.intervention: Doping the solid oxide fuel cell cathode material (e.g., PrBa0.5Sr0.5Co1.5Fe0.5O5+δ) with molybdenum (Mo) to form a Mo-doped layered double perovskite.

ranked.mechanism: Enhanced electrical conductivity and charge transfer kinetics in the doped cathode reduce Joule heating gradients and associated localized thermal stresses during operation, thereby mitigating thermal shock that leads to cracking.
ranked.intervention: Incorporating molybdenum into the cathode material to increase maximum electrical conductivity (targeting ~15% increase over undoped material).

ranked.mechanism: Atomic-scale modulation of oxygen vacancy formation energies stabilizes the crystal structure against thermal shock, reducing the driving force for microstructural degradation that initiates cracks.
ranked.intervention: Designing the cathode lattice to optimize oxygen vacancy formation energy through specific dopant selection (Mo), validated by density functional theory insights.
